stem: How is Layla’s perspective different from Yusuf’s at the start of the play?

stem: Why might a playwright include the stage direction “(the lights dim slowly)” at the end of a scene?

replace.new: To tell the actors to leave the stage immediately and go to the back room

stem: A paragraph about solar panels explains how sunlight, electrons, and wiring work together to create electricity, in that order. A reader mixes up the sequence. What is the best fix?

replace.old: Make up an order that sounds logical.
replace.new: Make up an order that sounds logical to the reader.

replace.old: Only reread the heading of the section.
replace.new: Only reread the heading of the section and then move on.

replace.new: Skip the paragraph entirely and read the next section instead.

stem: Read: “Coral reefs are home to thousands of species of fish. They form when tiny coral animals called polyps build hard skeletons over many years. Reefs also protect coastlines by slowing down powerful waves.” Which sentence BEST summarizes the whole passage?
correct: Coral reefs, built slowly by polyps, support ocean life and protect coastlines.

replace.old: Coral polyps are a type of fish.
replace.new: Coral polyps are a type of fish that live in the warm sea.

replace.old: Reefs form in just a few days.
replace.new: Reefs form in just a few days after a big storm hits the sea.

replace.old: Waves are the biggest danger to coral reefs.
replace.new: Waves are the biggest danger to coral reefs and to the small fish near them.

stem: How does Noura’s father seem to feel about leaving?
correct: Calm and caring, wanting to comfort Noura

replace.old: Angry that Noura came to the shore
replace.new: Angry that Noura came to the shore alone

replace.old: Uninterested in saying goodbye
replace.new: Uninterested in saying goodbye to anyone

replace.old: Frightened of the sea
replace.new: Frightened of the sea and its high waves

stem: A writer argues against a new highway, stating, “Every single person I asked at the grocery store opposes it, so clearly the whole town is against it.” What is the flaw here?
correct: A small, unrepresentative group cannot reliably stand for the opinion of an entire town.

replace.old: It focuses only on cost estimates.
replace.new: It focuses only on cost estimates and never talks about what people in town think.

replace.old: It fails to mention the highway at all.
replace.new: It fails to mention the highway at all, though the whole speech is about a road.

replace.old: It relies on a government report.
replace.new: It relies on a government report that was written by experts about the town.

stem: In a play, the audience watches a character accept a gift they do not know is a trick, because an earlier aside revealed the giver's true plan. What literary effect does this create?

replace.new: A plot twist that surprises the audience as well as the character when the gift is opened at the very end of the play.

replace.old: Suspense about what the gift physically looks like
replace.new: Suspense about what the gift physically looks like and who made it for the giver

stem: Read: "Despite her coach’s doubts about her chances, the swimmer kept believing she could qualify, trained before dawn every day, and shaved two full seconds off her best time at the trials." Which sentence best states the theme of this story?
correct: Believing in yourself helps you overcome doubt from others.

replace.old: Coaches are always right about their swimmers.
replace.new: Coaches are always right about their swimmers and their chances.

replace.old: Training before dawn guarantees success.
replace.new: Training before dawn guarantees success in every sport.

replace.old: Doubt from others always comes true.
replace.new: Doubt from others always comes true in the end.

stem: Which question CANNOT be answered from “Keeping Bees in the Mountains”?
correct: How many beekeepers live in the mountains?

replace.old: Where is the honey sold?
replace.new: Where is the honey sold in the mountains?

replace.new: Why do beekeepers use smoke around the hives?

stem: Read: “The principal announced that uniforms would now be required, calling it a step toward fairness among students. Yusra argued it would only hide the real differences in students' lives outside school.” How does Yusra's perspective differ from the principal's?
correct: Yusra believes uniforms only mask inequality rather than truly solving it, unlike the principal's view of fairness.

replace.new: Yusra has no opinion about the new uniform policy and never says a word about it in class.

replace.old: Yusra agrees that uniforms create true fairness among students.
replace.new: Yusra agrees that uniforms create true fairness among students, just as the principal says in her announcement.

stem: Read the sentences. “Adel's little sister asked him for the fifth time that afternoon to play outside, and each time he said he was too busy with his model airplane. correct: He felt a flicker of guilt about turning his sister away.

replace.old: He wanted to go outside himself.
replace.new: He wanted to go outside himself and play with his sister.

replace.new: He was waiting for a friend to arrive and help him build.

stem: What happens AFTER Nour searches her room?
correct: She remembers she read the book at the park.

replace.old: She notices the book is missing.
replace.new: She notices the book is missing from the shelf.

replace.old: She finds the book on the bench.
replace.new: She finds the book on the bench at the park.

stem: Which revision strengthens the plain sentence “The street market was busy and loud” with more vivid SENSORY imagery?
correct: Vendors shouted over clattering carts, and the smoky scent of grilled corn drifted between the stalls.

replace.new: People walked around the busy market quickly, and many of them stopped to look at the goods.

replace.new: The street market had many people and sounds, and it was a very busy place to be on a Friday afternoon.

stem: Which clause correctly links a counterclaim to a reason using “although”?

replace.new: Some families like uniforms and some do not, so each school can simply choose whatever is best for its own students, teachers and families.

stem: What is the central conflict at the beginning of the story?
correct: The governor wants Tarek's best jar for free, and Tarek must find a way to keep it.

stem: In “Transplant,” the tree “bowed its narrow head.” What does this personification suggest?
correct: The tree seemed sad and weak after being moved.

replace.old: The tree was angry.
replace.new: The tree was angry about being moved away.

replace.old: The tree was praying.
replace.new: The tree was praying for rain in the garden.

replace.old: The tree was growing fast.
replace.new: The tree was growing fast in its new spot.

stem: Read this paragraph: “Fishing fleets off one coastal town had been catching so many young sardines that the overall sardine population began shrinking every year. Marine officials introduced a seasonal catch limit and required nets with wider holes so young fish could escape. Within three years, sardine numbers in the area had begun to recover.” How is this paragraph organized?
correct: problem and solution — it names a shrinking-fish-population problem and the specific rules that helped fix it

replace.old: description — it only describes what a fishing net looks like
replace.new: description — it only describes what a fishing net looks like and how fishermen use it at sea

replace.old: compare and contrast — it compares sardine fishing to tuna fishing
replace.new: compare and contrast — it compares sardine fishing to tuna fishing in two different towns that are far apart

replace.old: chronological order — it lists every year’s exact catch numbers
replace.new: chronological order — it lists every year’s exact catch numbers from the first day to the last

stem: A speaker claims, “Everyone knows that students who play sports get worse grades,” without citing any source. What is the main issue with this argument?
correct: It presents an unsupported generalization as if it were an established fact.

replace.new: It fails to mention sports at all, even though the speaker talks about them.

replace.old: It focuses only on grades in one specific class.
replace.new: It focuses only on grades in one specific class and one teacher.

replace.old: It cites a peer-reviewed study.
replace.new: It cites a peer-reviewed study that was done by a team of doctors.

stem: Read: "The young falcon had practiced short flights from branch to branch all week and was now perched at the very top of the tall cliff." What will the falcon most likely do next?
correct: Attempt a longer flight from the cliff.

replace.old: Forget how to fly.
replace.new: Forget how to fly and stay in the nest.

replace.old: Stay on the branch forever.
replace.new: Stay on the branch forever and never move.

replace.old: Build a nest instead of flying.
replace.new: Build a nest instead of flying away.

stem: The desert hikers were relieved to find a small, hidden oasis with cool water and shady palm trees. What does oasis mean?
correct: a green, fertile area with water in the middle of a dry desert

replace.old: a type of desert animal
replace.new: a type of desert animal that lives under the sand

replace.old: a dangerous sandstorm
replace.new: a dangerous sandstorm that covers the camels and hikers in dust

replace.new: a sandy hill with no plants or water on the top of it

stem: Read this paragraph: “Many students who rode bikes to Al-Nour School left them leaning against the fence, where they often got knocked over or blocked the sidewalk. correct: problem and solution — it names a bike-parking problem and the specific solution the council proposed and the school carried out

replace.old: cause and effect — leaning bikes against the fence caused the fence to break
replace.new: cause and effect — leaning bikes against the fence caused the fence to break, which then caused many students to walk to school

replace.new: compare and contrast — it compares bike racks at two different schools and says which racks are better

replace.new: description — it only describes what the bikes looked like and what colors the students liked

stem: A watched pot never boils, Mama told Fadi as he stared at the stove waiting for dinner. What does this adage mean?
correct: Time seems to pass more slowly when you are anxiously waiting for something.

replace.old: Waiting always makes food taste better.
replace.new: Waiting always makes food taste better, so it is good to wait a long time.

replace.old: You should never watch food while it cooks.
replace.new: You should never watch food while it cooks, because it will burn if you look.

replace.new: Pots boil faster if no one watches them, because the heat likes to be alone.

stem: Read this paragraph: “Volunteers at an animal shelter noticed that many dogs stayed longer when their photos online looked blurry or dark. correct: Improving online photos and descriptions helped shelter dogs get adopted much faster.

replace.old: The shelter stopped posting photos of dogs online entirely.
replace.new: The shelter stopped posting photos of dogs online entirely and used only paper signs.

replace.old: Dogs with blurry photos were adopted faster than other dogs.
replace.new: Dogs with blurry photos were adopted faster than all other dogs.

stem: Why does Layla mention “what Dad said”?

replace.old: She wants Karim to call their dad.
replace.new: She wants Karim to call their dad and ask him for help.

replace.old: She is changing the subject to calm down.
replace.new: She is changing the subject to calm down and avoid a fight.

stem: Read this paragraph: “A community garden project initially struggled because most plots sat empty during the hottest summer weeks, when volunteers avoided working outside. correct: Rescheduling garden work around the hottest hours fixed most of the staffing problem, though a few especially hot plots stayed harder to maintain.

replace.old: The shadeless plots were the only ones that were ever used.
replace.new: The shadeless plots were the only ones that were ever used, and volunteers refused to touch every other plot in the whole garden for the entire year.

replace.new: Changing the schedule solved every single staffing problem completely, and no plot was ever empty again after that summer.

replace.old: Volunteers avoided the garden entirely, even after the schedule changed.
replace.new: Volunteers avoided the garden entirely, even after the schedule changed, and the project was closed at the end of the season.

stem: Read this paragraph: “Many recycling programs found that bins meant only for paper and plastic were filled with food waste, greasy pizza boxes and broken glass, ruining otherwise recyclable material. replace.old: description only — it simply describes what is typically found inside a recycling bin
replace.new: description only — it simply describes what is typically found inside a recycling bin, from plastic bottles to paper boxes and cans, and says nothing about any problem

replace.old: chronological order only — it lists each city’s recycling program by the year it was founded

replace.old: compare and contrast only — it compares recycling rules in different countries
replace.new: compare and contrast only — it compares recycling rules in different countries, showing which country has the strictest rules

stem: How does the flashback affect the story's structure?

replace.old: pure chronological order — it lists the exact hour each city planted its first tree
